acceptedAnswer.text: Signing up, the API key and a small free allowance to try it. GET /v1/billing/tier, with your key, says what your account allows and what is left, and every answer carries X-RateLimit-Remaining. A person on the Free plan gets free model requests and Kai decisions; the request after the allowance answers 429 until its window resets.

mainEntity.name: What does it cost after that?

acceptedAnswer.text: You pay as you go from the balance you top up: each call is billed at its model’s rate in GET /v1/pricing, and GET /v1/billing/plans lists every plan for people with its price.

mainEntity.name: Can an agent sign up without a person?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. With a wallet it needs no inbox and no person: it signs a one-time challenge from hanzo.id, a first-seen wallet gets its own account and organization, and it mints a key with the token it gets back. The whole flow is the script above. An agent with an inbox can sign up by email code instead, and one with neither has its person approve a device code once.

Over the API in stablecoins: GET /v1/billing/crypto/options lists the chains (today Base, Ethereum and Solana) and the tokens (USDC and USDT) the rail accepts, POST /v1/billing/crypto/deposit returns the address to send to, and GET /v1/billing/crypto/deposit/{id} says when it is credited. Cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay go through the checkout at hanzo.ai/pay, which needs a browser.

mainEntity.name: How do I keep an agent from overspending?

acceptedAnswer.text: Give each agent its own key with a monthly budget in cents and a rate in requests a minute: past the budget a call answers 402, past the rate 429. A session can carry its own cap, set with POST /v1/agent/sessions/{id}/budget, and a session that reaches it pauses until the cap is raised.

mainEntity.name: Which tools can my agent use?

acceptedAnswer.text: The native Hanzo MCP server, over stdio from one line in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Zed: npx -y hanzo mcp. It carries the Kai decision tools beside files, shell, git, code search, the browser and the computer.
